subject: physics
question_text: Derive the equation s = ut + ½at² using the graphical method.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Motion in a Straight Line · 4 marks

steps.label: The v–t graph
steps.why: A body with uniform acceleration has a straight-line v–t graph, so the area under it is a trapezium that splits into one rectangle and one triangle.
common_mistakes: Drawing a curved line. Uniform acceleration gives a straight line.
Leaving the graph unlabelled, which loses the mark even when the shape is right.

recall.must_convey: That the graph is a straight line from A at velocity u to B at velocity v over time t.

steps.memory_tip: Uniform acceleration means a STRAIGHT v–t line. Label O, A, B, C, D.
steps.margin_note: Draw it first. The figure is one of the four marks.

steps.label: Area = displacement
lines: For a velocity–time graph, the area under the
So s = area of the trapezium OABD.
steps.why: Velocity multiplied by time is displacement, and that product is exactly what an area on a v–t graph measures.
common_mistakes: Saying the SLOPE gives displacement. The slope gives acceleration; the area gives displacement.

recall.must_convey: That the area under a velocity time graph is the displacement.

steps.memory_tip: Area = displacement. Slope = acceleration. Two different features, two different meanings.
steps.margin_note: State the rule before using it.

steps.label: The two areas
lines: Split OABD into rectangle OACD and △ABC:
area OACD = OA × OD = u t
area ABC = ½ × AC × BC = ½ × t × (v − u)

lines.text: and v − u = at, so area ABC = ½ a t²

steps.why: The rectangle is the distance the body would have covered at its starting speed; the triangle is the extra distance the acceleration added.
common_mistakes: Using BC = v instead of BC = v − u. The triangle sits above the rectangle.

recall.must_convey: That the rectangle has area u t and the triangle has area half a t squared, using v minus u equals a t.
accept: v minus u is a t

steps.memory_tip: Rectangle = what u alone would give. Triangle = what a adds on top.
steps.margin_note: Substituting v − u = at is the step that makes ½at² appear.

steps.label: The result
steps.why: The two areas add because they are two parts of one trapezium, so the displacement is the sum of the steady part and the accelerated part.
common_mistakes: Writing s = ut + ½at, missing the square on t.

recall.must_convey: That s equals u t plus half a t squared.
accept: u t plus half a t squared
reject: u t plus half a t

insider_note: A 3-star cell. The figure carries a mark on its own — draw and label the v–t graph before any algebra.
